title: Window Rebates in Halifax 2026: $30 per Opening, Honest Math
desc: Efficiency Nova Scotia pays $30 per ENERGY STAR window or door opening in Halifax, through a home assessment. Why that is small, and which upgrades pay more for the same money.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Halifax
lead: Halifax homeowners can get a rebate on new windows and doors, but it is small: $30 per opening through Efficiency Nova Scotia's Home Energy Assessment. Here is how it works, what a typical house would get, and when the money is better spent elsewhere.
cards_heading: What window rebates pay in Halifax
cards_intro: From Efficiency Nova Scotia's Home Energy Assessment rebate guide (August 2026), still linked from its program page on October 3, 2026.

cards.title: ENERGY STAR windows and doors
cards.note: Through the Home Energy Assessment. Paid per opening you replace with an ENERGY STAR certified product.

cards.title: Air sealing
cards.note: Often the cheaper way to stop the drafts people blame on windows.

cards.title: Assessment total
cards.note: Window money counts toward the same $5,000 cap as insulation and heat pumps.

after_cards:
The honest math

A Halifax house replacing 12 windows and 2 doors has 14 rough openings. At $30 each, that is $420. New windows for a whole house cost far more than that, so the rebate covers a small slice. If your windows are failing (rot, broken seals, fogging), replace them and take the $420. If they are just old, compare them with the insulation and air sealing in your assessment report first.
sections: What counts as a rough opening

A rough opening is the framed hole in the wall that a window or door sits in. Efficiency Nova Scotia counts the openings you replace with ENERGY STAR certified products and pays $30 for each. Doors count too, as long as the product is ENERGY STAR certified. Ask your window supplier for the certification and keep the paperwork for your final assessment.

About 45% of Halifax households live in homes built before 1981, according to Statistics Canada's 2021 Census. If your windows are original to a house that age, they are the ones most likely to be due. About 8% of Halifax households live in homes built before 1946, where windows can be part of a home's character. Refurbishing and adding storm windows may suit those houses better than full replacement.

Renters can't claim this rebate, because the homeowner must book the assessment. That leaves out a large share of Halifax: 42% of households rent.
When to do windows, and when to wait

Do the assessment before you sign a window contract. The advisor's report shows where your house actually loses heat. If it points to the attic or basement, those rebates are bigger: up to $750 for the attic and $1,200 for basement walls. Air sealing pays $200 and can stop drafts around frames for much less than new windows. If you are planning a heat pump too, doing the shell first can let you buy a smaller unit.

If your household income is lower, HomeWarming may cover draft-proofing and insulation at no charge. Moderate-income homes heated with oil or propane can get up to $5,000 more through the Moderate Income Rebate, with pre-approval.
Why Nova Scotia's window rebate looks small

If you have read about window rebates elsewhere, Nova Scotia's will look low. In British Columbia, BC Hydro and FortisBC pay $100 per window or door, up to $2,000. Efficiency Nova Scotia's bigger amounts go to heat pumps, insulation and free upgrades for lower-income homes instead. That is a good hint about where your own money goes furthest in a Nova Scotia house, and why the assessment report is worth reading before you order anything.
claim_heading: How to get the window rebate in Halifax
claim_steps: Book a Home Energy Assessment before you order windows ($199, or free if your income qualifies).
Read the report. Compare window replacement with the insulation and air sealing it recommends.
Buy ENERGY STAR certified windows and doors, and keep the certification paperwork.
Finish the installation within 12 months of your first assessment.
Book the final assessment so the advisor can count your new openings.
faq: How much is the window rebate in Halifax?
$30 per rough opening for ENERGY STAR certified windows and doors, through Efficiency Nova Scotia's Home Energy Assessment.
Do I need an assessment for the window rebate?
Yes. The window rebate is paid only through the Home Energy Assessment, with a visit before the work and a final visit after.
Is it worth replacing windows for the rebate?
Not for the rebate alone. It covers a small part of the cost. Replace windows that are failing, and compare them with the insulation and air sealing your assessment recommends.
Do doors count for the Nova Scotia window rebate?
Yes. ENERGY STAR certified exterior doors count as rough openings at $30 each.
